_schema: The standard motor configuration grid behind the Motor Designer (Decided #1): stator size x the KV options sold for that size x the pole configuration the size uses. Every combination is allowed; there is no turns or wire-gauge input. Rm, Io, Kt, mass and max current are NOT stored per motor: they are derived by formulas from stator volume and KV (see src/propulsion/motor_configs.gd), using the coefficients below. Every coefficient has basis "est." (a class-typical fit, not a measurement and not a datasheet value) and a note saying what it was anchored to. Nothing here is a measurement of a motor on a bench; all derived figures are ideal / model figures. Size rows: stator_diameter_mm and stator_height_mm are read from the size name (2306.5 = 23 mm x 6.5 mm); config is the slot/pole pair (9N12P = 9 slots 12 poles); kv_options lists the KV values commonly listed for that stator size (basis est.: representative of vendor catalogs, no single source, and not an exhaustive list of every motor sold); max_cells is the largest pack the class is normally flown on (est.); io_voltage_v is the voltage at which Io is stated (est.; Io scales with rpm as in MotorModel.io_at_rpm). shaft_mm_options and mount_options (est.: representative of vendor catalogs for the size; the first entry is the size's usual one) are the designer's Bell & shaft choices; the first shaft is the one mass_base_g already allows for.

rm_c.note: Rm = rm_c / (V_cm3^(5/3) * Kv^2), ohm. Kv*Kt-style winding law: Rm scales as 1/Kv^2 at fixed stator; 5/3 exponent is geometric scaling of the motor constant (Km ~ L^2.5). Anchor: a 2207 1750KV near 0.06 ohm. Anchor value is a class-typical figure, not a datasheet. 2026-11-03: raised 940000 -> 1128000 (x1.2) after MOTOR_RM_IO_CHECK.md measured estimates at 0.6-1.0x (median 0.8x) of published Rm; shop-listed Rm is +/-30% noise.

io_k.note: Io(A) = io_k * V_cm3 * (Kv * io_voltage_v / 10000). Iron and friction loss grow with stator volume and rpm. Anchor: a 2207 1750KV near 1.0 A at 10 V.

mass_base_g.note: mass_g = mass_base_g + mass_per_cm3_g * V_cm3. Bell, shaft, bearings and base as a size-independent allowance. Fitted by eye to the shelf's 0802 3.2 g, 2207 32 g, 2807 52 g (data/parts/motors.json); small 14xx motors weigh more than this line.

mass_per_cm3_g.note: Grams of stator, copper, magnets and bell per cm3 of stator volume. Same fit as mass_base_g.

loss_w_per_g23.note: Continuous dissipation the motor can shed, W = loss_w_per_g23 * mass_g^(2/3) (surface area law). Max continuous current = sqrt(that / Rm). Anchor: a 2207 1750KV near 35 A continuous. Tiny motors (08xx) come out higher than their published 3-5 A ratings.

copper_mass_fraction.note: Share of motor mass that is winding copper; feeds the thermal mass.

stator_mass_fraction.note: Share of motor mass that is stator iron; feeds the thermal mass.

nominal_cell_v.note: Used only for max_power_w: max continuous current at max_cells x 3.7 V.

io_pole_exponent.note: Io scales as (poles / size's usual poles)^io_pole_exponent when the builder picks the other pole config: iron (hysteresis) loss grows with electrical frequency, which is rpm x pole pairs. 1.0 is the hysteresis-only case; eddy loss would push it higher.

shaft_density_g_cm3.note: Steel. A shaft other than the size's usual one changes mass by density x pi/4 x (d^2 - d0^2) x length, length = bell height + 8 mm.
